Validate an absolute risk model in a cohort or a sample from a cohort

Source: R/model_validation.R
ModelValidation.Rd

Assesses the calibration and discrimination of an absolute risk model in independent data from a cohort study (full cohort) or from a sample drawn from a cohort with known inclusion probabilities, such as a nested case-control study. Risks are validated over a fixed interval after study entry (e.g. 5-year risks) or over each subject's observed follow-up.

The function reports

  • calibration in the large: the ratio of the expected to the observed number of cases (E/O) with its confidence interval;

  • calibration by risk group: subjects are grouped by their risk score (deciles by default), and the observed and expected absolute risks, relative risks and E/O ratios of the groups are compared, with a Hosmer-Lemeshow test of the absolute risks and a test of the relative risks;

  • discrimination: the area under the ROC curve (AUC) of the risk score;

  • the study's incidence rates by attained age, to compare with the population incidence rates of the model.

Usage

ModelValidation(
  study.data,
  total.followup.validation = FALSE,
  predicted.risk = NULL,
  predicted.risk.interval = NULL,
  linear.predictor = NULL,
  iCARE.model.object = list(model.formula = NULL, model.cov.info = NULL, model.snp.info =
    NULL, model.log.RR = NULL, model.ref.dataset = NULL, model.ref.dataset.weights =
    NULL, model.disease.incidence.rates = NULL, model.competing.incidence.rates = NULL,
    model.bin.fh.name = NA, apply.cov.profile = NULL, apply.snp.profile = NULL, n.imp =
    5),
  number.of.percentiles = 10,
  reference.entry.age = NULL,
  reference.exit.age = NULL,
  predicted.risk.ref = NULL,
  linear.predictor.ref = NULL,
  linear.predictor.cutoffs = NULL,
  dataset = "Example Dataset",
  model.name = "Example Risk Prediction Model",
  hosmer.lemeshow.variance = c("expected", "observed")
)

Arguments

study.data

Data frame with one row per subject and the columns

  • observed.outcome: 1 if the disease developed during follow-up, 0 otherwise;

  • study.entry.age: age at entry into the study;

  • study.exit.age: age at the last follow-up;

  • time.of.onset: years from entry to disease onset (Inf or NA for subjects without the disease);

  • sampling.weights (optional): for a sample from the cohort, such as a nested case-control study, each subject's probability of inclusion in the sample.

total.followup.validation

If TRUE, validate risks over each subject's observed follow-up; if FALSE (default), over predicted.risk.interval.

predicted.risk

Optional vector of predicted absolute risks, one per subject. If NULL, the risks are computed from iCARE.model.object.

predicted.risk.interval

Years after entry over which risks are validated (e.g. 5): one value, or one per subject. Not used when total.followup.validation = TRUE.

linear.predictor

Optional vector of risk scores (the linear predictor \(x'\beta\)), one per subject. If NULL, computed from iCARE.model.object. A supplied predicted.risk or linear.predictor is always used as given; only a missing one is computed.

iCARE.model.object

Named list of arguments of computeAbsoluteRisk() describing the model and the subjects: model.formula, model.cov.info, model.snp.info, model.log.RR, model.ref.dataset, model.ref.dataset.weights, model.disease.incidence.rates, model.competing.incidence.rates, model.bin.fh.name, apply.cov.profile and apply.snp.profile (the subjects' risk factors, one row per row of study.data) and n.imp. Settings that earlier versions needed here (use.c.code, return.lp, return.refs.risk) are accepted and ignored.

number.of.percentiles

Number of risk-score groups formed at quantiles of the risk score (default 10, deciles).

reference.entry.age, reference.exit.age

Optional ages (one value, or one per row of model.ref.dataset) over which to compute the absolute risks of the reference population, returned as Reference_Absolute_Risk.

predicted.risk.ref, linear.predictor.ref

Optional absolute risks and risk scores of the reference population, returned as given.

linear.predictor.cutoffs

Optional cut points of the risk score defining the risk groups, instead of quantiles.

dataset, model.name

Names of the dataset and the model, shown by print() and plotModelValidation().

hosmer.lemeshow.variance

Variance in the Hosmer-Lemeshow statistic: "expected" (default) or "observed" (earlier versions); see Details.

Value

An object of class "icareValid": a list with

  • Subject_Specific_Observed_Outcome, Adjusted_Followup: outcome and follow-up over the risk prediction interval;

  • Risk_Prediction_Interval: the interval, e.g. "5 years" or "Observed Followup";

  • Subject_Specific_Predicted_Absolute_Risk, Subject_Specific_Risk_Score: each subject's predicted risk and risk score;

  • Reference_Absolute_Risk, Reference_Risk_Score: those of the reference population (NULL unless supplied or requested);

  • Population_Incidence_Rate: the model's disease incidence rates;

  • Study_Incidence_Rate: data frame of the study's incidence rates by attained age (ages, study_incidence), their confidence limits (lower, upper), and the (weighted) cases and person_years;

  • Category_Results: data frame with one row per risk-score group: the group (Categories); its observed and predicted absolute risks and relative risks with confidence intervals for the observed ones; its E/O ratio with confidence interval (Expected_to_Observed_Ratio, CI_Expected_to_Observed_Ratio_Lower, CI_Expected_to_Observed_Ratio_Upper); and its numbers of subjects and cases in the data;

  • Category_Specific_Observed_Absolute_Risk, Category_Specific_Predicted_Absolute_Risk, Category_Specific_Observed_Relative_Risk, Category_Specific_Predicted_Relative_Risk, Category_Specific_Expected_to_Observed_Ratio: the same, as vectors;

  • Variance_Matrix_Absolute_Risk, Variance_Matrix_LogRelative_Risk: covariance matrices of the groups' observed absolute risks and log relative risks;

  • Hosmer_Lemeshow_Results, HL_pvalue: the Hosmer-Lemeshow test (an htest object) and its p-value;

  • RR_test_result, RR_test_pvalue: the relative-risk test and its p-value;

  • AUC, Variance_AUC, CI_AUC: the AUC, its variance and 95% confidence interval;

  • Overall_Expected_to_Observed_Ratio, CI_Overall_Expected_to_Observed_Ratio: E/O and its 95% confidence interval;

  • input.args: the model formula, the study data, the names and the settings, used by print() and plot().

Details

Follow-up. Each subject is followed from study.entry.age for the shorter of the risk prediction interval and the observed follow-up, and counts as a case only if the disease develops within that time (Adjusted_Followup, Subject_Specific_Observed_Outcome). When the risks are computed here, each subject's risk covers that same time from study.entry.age, so that a subject followed for 3 years of a 5-year interval contributes a 3-year risk. To validate fixed-horizon risks, compute them yourself and supply predicted.risk and linear.predictor. Cases whose onset is recorded after exit are treated as non-cases censored at exit, with a warning.

Sampled data. When study.data has a sampling.weights column (each subject's probability of inclusion in the sample), all estimates are weighted by the inverse probabilities, and the variances add the variability due to sampling.

Risk-score groups. Subjects are grouped at quantiles of linear.predictor (weighted quantiles in sampled data), or at linear.predictor.cutoffs. Values tied at a quantile form their own group, and groups left empty are dropped; the tests use the number of groups actually formed, \(G\).

Tests. The Hosmer-Lemeshow statistic is \(\sum_g (O_g - E_g)^2 / V_g\) on \(G\) degrees of freedom, where \(O_g\) and \(E_g\) are the observed and expected absolute risks of group \(g\). With hosmer.lemeshow.variance = "expected" (the default), \(V_g\) is the variance under the null hypothesis of calibration, \(E_g(1 - E_g)/N_g\) (plus a sampling term in sampled data), as in the classical Hosmer-Lemeshow test. With "observed", \(V_g\) is the variance of \(O_g\), as in earlier versions of iCARE; that test rejects too often when groups have few cases and is infinite when a group has none. The relative-risk test compares the observed and expected relative risks of the groups (each group's risk divided by the mean over groups) by a Wald test of the log relative risks on \(G - 1\) degrees of freedom; it needs a case in every group. Like the "observed" Hosmer-Lemeshow test, it rejects a calibrated model too often when groups have few cases. In simulations at the 5% level, it rejected 11.5% of the time with 10 cases per group on average, 7.7% with 30 and 6.7% with 50 (see vignette("model-validation")). With few cases, form fewer groups.

Confidence intervals are 95% Wald intervals: on the log scale for E/O ratios and relative risks, and on the risk scale for absolute risks and the AUC. The E/O interval in a full cohort treats the expected risks as known; in sampled data it also accounts for the sampling variability of the expected risk and its covariance with the observed risk.

AUC. The probability that a case has a higher risk score than a non-case, counting ties as 1/2, weighted by the inverse inclusion probabilities in sampled data, with the variance of DeLong et al. (1988). The risk score is the linear predictor, which excludes age, so the AUC measures discrimination by the risk factors within the age distribution of the study.

Study incidence. Onsets divided by person-years at each year of attained age over the observed follow-up, with exact Poisson intervals in a full cohort and weighted estimates with Wald intervals in sampled data.

References

Pal Choudhury P, Maas P, Wilcox A, et al. (2020). iCARE: An R package to build, validate and apply absolute risk models. PLOS ONE 15(2): e0228198. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0228198

DeLong ER, DeLong DM, Clarke-Pearson DL (1988). Comparing the areas under two or more correlated receiver operating characteristic curves: a nonparametric approach. Biometrics 44(3): 837-845.

Hosmer DW, Lemeshow S (1980). Goodness of fit tests for the multiple logistic regression model. Communications in Statistics - Theory and Methods 9(10): 1043-1069.

See also

plotModelValidation(), computeAbsoluteRisk()

Examples

data(bc_data, package = "iCARE")

# 5-year risks in a random sample of the full validation cohort
set.seed(50)
cohort <- validation.cohort.data[sample(nrow(validation.cohort.data), 5000), ]
covariates <- all.vars(bc_model_formula)[-1]
validation <- ModelValidation(
  study.data = cohort,
  predicted.risk.interval = 5,
  iCARE.model.object = list(
    model.formula = bc_model_formula,
    model.cov.info = bc_model_cov_info,
    model.log.RR = bc_model_log_or,
    model.ref.dataset = ref_cov_dat,
    model.disease.incidence.rates = bc_inc,
    model.competing.incidence.rates = mort_inc,
    apply.cov.profile = cohort[, covariates]
  ),
  dataset = "Simulated cohort",
  model.name = "Breast cancer risk model"
)
validation
